title: Cristaux et cohomologie de De Rham : généralités, correspondances Deligne et Berthelot (1965-1969) : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
This is an elementary scratch computation of Legendre's formula for the p-adic valuation of n!.

Notation: throughout the page v_p(p^k) is shorthand for v_p((p^k)!), and v_p(1)=0 means v_p(1!)=0.

Setup. Write n = a_0 + a_1 p + ... + a_ν p^ν in base p. The first lines try to reduce v_p(n!) to a combination Σ a_k v_p((p^k)!). This is legitimate because v_p((m+p^k)!) - v_p(m!) = v_p((p^k)!) when m is a multiple of p^{k+1}.

Recursion. The second line gives
v_p((p^{μ+1})!) = (μ+1) + (p-1)[v_p((p^μ)!) + ... + v_p(p!)].
Two ways to see it:
- Peel off one block of size p^μ at a time. The last element p^{μ+1} contributes μ+1.
- Equivalently, subtract consecutive cases of the closed formula.

Small cases checked by hand:
- v_p(p!) = 1.
- v_p((p^2)!) = 2 + (p-1) = p+1.
- v_p((p^3)!) = 3 + (p-1)(p+2) = p^2+p+1.
- v_p((p^4)!) = 4 + (p-1)(p^2+2p+3) = p^3+p^2+p+1.

General case. The guess is v_p((p^ν)!) = 1+p+...+p^{ν-1} = (p^ν-1)/(p-1). Induction uses Σ_{k=1}^{ν}(p^k-1)/(p-1) = p^{ν-1} + 2p^{ν-2} + ... + ν. Multiplying by (p-1) telescopes, giving v_p((p^{ν+1})!) = 1+p+...+p^ν.

Conclusion. Summing,
(p-1) v_p(n!) = Σ a_k (p^k-1) = n - Σ a_k,
hence v_p(n!) = (n - s_p(n))/(p-1), where s_p(n) is the base-p digit sum.

Purpose (in the crystals / de Rham context of this folder). Such estimates control divided powers x^n/n!: the p-adic size of γ_n, convergence of exponential-type series, and the bounds v_p(n!) ≤ (n-1)/(p-1) and v_p(n!) < n/(p-1). These are standard in crystalline cohomology.

The handwriting and the neighbouring pages, which are typescript-like text on divisors and heights on abelian varieties, suggest this is a stray scratch sheet; it may not even be by Grothendieck.
errors: Notation abuse: v_p(p^k) is written for v_p((p^k)!). Read literally it would be k.
The final formula writes Σ a_i; the derivation shows it must include a_0, i.e. the full digit sum s_p(n). The line n - a_0 - a_1 - ... - a_ν is correct.
The partial line 'a_1 + p a_2 + p^2 a_3' is an abandoned regrouping and is not used.

ideas.what: Closed formula v_p((p^ν)!) = (p^ν-1)/(p-1), obtained via a recursion over k-adic blocks

ideas.where_published: standard; used implicitly in Berthelot's crystalline cohomology for divided-power estimates

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine scratch derivation of Legendre's classical formula, presumably to estimate divided powers p-adically. Nothing new or uncredited.
transcription_corrections: Throughout, 'v_p(p^k)' should be read as v_p((p^k)!).
The v_p(p^3) line reads 3 + (p-1)(p+1+1) = p^2+p+1. The '(p+2' is crossed out and replaced by (p-1)(p+1+1).
The crossed-out symbol under the brace in the second line is p^{μ+1} (or p^μ), deleted.
The v_p(p^4) line contains a crossed-out stray term before p^3+p^2+p+1.
The first line reads v_p(n!) = a_ν v_p((p^ν)!) + ... + a_{μ+1} v_p((p^{μ+1})!); the superscript on v is crossed out.
